content_text:
At 24/25 fps at ISO 100:
100 fc = f/2.8
200 fc = f/4
400 fc = f/5.6
800 fc = f/8
So with ISO 800:
100 fc = f/8
200 fc = f/11
400 fc = f/16
You lose 5-stops going from 25 fps to 800 fps, so to shoot at f/2.8, you need to light for f/16 so that once you lose 5-stops by going from 25 fps to 800 fps, you’re down to f/2.8.
